summary: Oil retreated and Treasury yields eased. Stocks approached records as lower cost pressure met strong profit expectations.

markets.name: S&P 500
markets.description: The S&P 500 tracks large U.S. companies and approached a record. Lower oil and bond yields eased pressure on business costs and stock valuations.

explains.anchor_text: Lower oil and bond yields eased pressure
explains.why: Cheaper energy can reduce operating costs, while lower yields reduce the return stocks must compete with.
explains.other_reading: Strong profit expectations also supported prices, and intraday gains can reverse.

markets.range: Approximate level derived from the reported 0.8% move

markets.name: 10-year Treasury yield
markets.description: The 10-year Treasury yield, a benchmark for longer-term borrowing, eased from Monday's multi-decade high. Mortgages and business loans may still remain expensive, as lenders add risk and servicing costs.

explains.anchor_text: Mortgages and business loans may still remain expensive
explains.why: Lenders often begin with a Treasury benchmark, then add compensation for credit risk, servicing, and profit.
explains.other_reading: Competition and borrower quality can move individual loan rates differently.

markets.name: Brent crude oil
markets.description: Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, moved lower. Sustained declines can reduce fuel, freight, and packaging pressure, though refining and distribution still shape household prices.

explains.anchor_text: reduce fuel, freight, and packaging pressure
explains.why: Oil feeds transportation and petroleum-based materials used across supply chains.
explains.other_reading: Refining margins, taxes, inventories, and contracts can delay or offset the change.

markets.range: Down from nearly $110 several weeks earlier

markets.name: Nasdaq Composite
markets.description: The Nasdaq Composite, with substantial technology exposure, extended Monday's record. Lower yields can support highly valued companies whose expected profits sit farther in the future.

explains.anchor_text: Lower yields can support highly valued companies
explains.why: A lower discount rate raises the present value assigned to future profits.
explains.other_reading: Company earnings and investor positioning can outweigh interest-rate moves.

markets.range: Approximate level derived from the reported 0.8% move

markets.name: Dow Jones Industrial Average
markets.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average tracks 30 established U.S. companies. Its rise showed that Tuesday's gains extended beyond technology shares.

explains.why: The Dow contains industrial, financial, health-care, and consumer companies with less technology concentration than the Nasdaq.
explains.other_reading: Thirty companies cannot represent every part of the economy.

markets.range: Up about 265 points at 11 a.m. ET

markets.name: Expected volatility
markets.description: The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX), a measure of expected stock-market swings, remained subdued even as stocks, oil, and bonds moved sharply.

explains.why: The index reflects prices for near-term S&P 500 options, which were not signaling severe stress.
explains.other_reading: A low level does not rule out a sudden market move.

calendar.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
calendar.definition: A measure of price changes for goods and services purchased by households.
calendar.hot: A higher-than-expected reading has often been associated with greater interest-rate pressure.
calendar.cool: A lower-than-expected reading has often been associated with less interest-rate pressure.

calendar.title: Producer Price Index (PPI)
calendar.definition: A measure of price changes received by domestic producers before many costs reach consumers.
calendar.hot: A higher-than-expected reading has often been associated with concern about future consumer-price pressure.
calendar.cool: A lower-than-expected reading has often been associated with easing business-cost pressure.

calendar.time: Decision at 2:00 p.m. ET on Oct. 28
calendar.title: Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting
calendar.definition: The Federal Reserve group that sets the target range for short-term interest rates.
calendar.hot: A tighter decision has often been associated with higher short-term borrowing costs.
calendar.cool: An unchanged rate has often been associated with more time for officials to assess inflation and employment.
